plain: To state something firmly as true.

webster.text: To affirm positively; to declare with assurance; to aver.

more.text: To maintain or defend by words or measures; to vindicate a claim or title to; as, to assert our rights and liberties.

example.quote: They went no farther than to assert the rights of the house; they courted no reply; and it ought not to be supposed they could give any offence.
example.cite: James Madison, Speech in Congress on the Jay Treaty, Apr. 6, 1796
